external.title: Connect to rustuya-bridge
external.description: The MQTT broker your running rustuya-bridge uses, and the IL prefix to publish under. Setup checks that the bridge answers there. The rest (topic root, IL source, device file) starts at its default; change it later in the Rustuya panel's Settings.

data_description.il_prefix: Where the devices are published for il-ha (or any IL consumer); il-ha reads il by default.

embedded.title: Run rustuya-bridge here
embedded.description: This still connects to a real MQTT broker; it just launches and owns the bridge process itself instead of you running one separately. Its topic root, state file and log level start at their defaults; change them later in the Rustuya panel's Settings.

data_description.il_prefix: Where the devices are published for il-ha (or any IL consumer); il-ha reads il by default.

onboard.title: Devices
onboard.description: Fetch your device list from Tuya Cloud now and register devices on the bridge (a saved login is used as is; otherwise you log in with a QR code). You can also do it later from the integration's Configure, or point at a device file rustuya-manager already keeps from the Rustuya panel's Settings.

menu_options.cloud_wizard_start: Fetch devices from Tuya Cloud now

cloud_wizard_start.title: Fetch devices from Tuya Cloud
cloud_wizard_start.description: A saved Tuya login is used as is. Without one (or when it has expired), a QR code to scan follows: the user code is only needed for that first login, from Smart Life → Me → Settings → Account and Security. To set up without fetching, close this window: Rustuya is added, and the fetch is in its Configure later.

data.user_code: User code (only for a new login)

cloud_wizard_scan.title: Scan the QR code
cloud_wizard_scan.description: There is no saved Tuya login (or it has expired): scan with the Smart Life or Tuya Smart app, then submit. Close this window to finish the setup without the fetch.

sync_devices.title: Sync devices with the bridge
sync_devices.description: Cloud list vs. what the bridge holds: {synced} in sync, {missing} missing from the bridge, {mismatched} with differing settings, {orphaned} on the bridge but not in the cloud list. Every device is listed with its state; nothing is changed unless you select it. {error}

data.update: Update on the bridge (push the cloud's settings)
data.remove: Remove from the bridge (any device it holds)

error.bridge_not_found: The broker answers, but no rustuya-bridge is running on that topic root. Start the bridge, or enter the topic root it runs on, and try again.
error.cannot_connect: Could not connect to the MQTT broker. Check the host, port and credentials.
error.invalid_prefix: An MQTT topic without wildcards (+, #) or empty levels, e.g. il or home/il.
error.publish_failed: Could not send the command to the bridge.
error.pyrustuyabridge_missing: pyrustuyabridge is not installed; pick an external bridge instead

abort.manager_busy: Another Tuya Cloud fetch or device sync window is still open. Close it and try again.
abort.single_instance_allowed: Rustuya is already set up; it runs as a single instance.

send_command.name: Send a command
send_command.description: Writes one raw data point to a Tuya device through the bridge, bypassing IL. Fire and forget: nothing checks the value or waits for the device. Locks, alarms and garage doors are refused unless their remote control is allowed in the options.

device_id.name: Device ID
device_id.description: The Tuya device ID (as in the device list), or the Home Assistant device an IL consumer such as il-ha made of it.

value.name: Value
value.description: The raw value: true/false, a number or a string.

unknown_device.message: Device {device_id} is not on the bridge (or not in the device list).

hazardous.message: Device {device_id} is a lock, alarm or garage door; allow their remote control in the options to send it commands.
